  (:require
   [ardoq.core :as core]
   [ardoq.persistence.component-type-repo :as component-type-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.model-repo :as model-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.model-template-repo :as model-template-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres-entity :as entity]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.branch.context :as branch-context]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.branch.tables :as branch-tables]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.postgres :as pg]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.postgres-query :as pq]
   [ardoq.persistence.reference-type-repo :as reference-type-repo]
   [ardoq.specs :as specs]
   [ardoq.utils.component-type-util :as component-type-util]
   [ardoq.utils.model-utils :as model-util]
   [ardoq.utils.reference-type-util :as reference-type-util]
   [honey.sql.helpers :as hh]
   [medley.core :as medley]
   [superstring.core :as str]))

(defn inconsistent-component-type-hierarchies [ctx]
  (->> (entity/query! model-repo/config ctx pq/all)
       (mapcat model-util/bad-type-hierarchy?)))

(defn unused-models [ctx]
  (entity/query! model-repo/config ctx
                 [:not [:in :_id (-> (hh/select :componentModel)
                                     (hh/from :workspace))]]))

(defn component-types-only-in-model! [ctx]
  (pg/execute! (:org-ds ctx)
               (if (branch-context/on-master? ctx)
                 (-> (hh/select :model :typeId)
                     (hh/from :component_type_view)
                     (hh/where [:not [:in [:composite :model :typeId]
                                      (-> (hh/select :modelId :id)
                                          (hh/from :component_type))]]))
                 (-> (hh/select :model :typeId)
                     (hh/from :branched_component_type_view)
                     (hh/where (pq/and (branch-tables/by-branch-id ctx)
                                       [:not [:in [:composite :model :typeId branch-tables/branch-column]
                                              (-> (hh/select :modelId :id branch-tables/branch-column)
                                                  (hh/from :branched_component_type))]]))))))

(defn component-types-not-in-model! [ctx]
  (pg/execute! (:org-ds ctx)
               (if (branch-context/on-master? ctx)
                 (-> (hh/select [:modelId :model] [:id :typeId])
                     (hh/from :component_type)
                     (hh/where [:not [:in [:composite :modelId :id]
                                      (-> (hh/select :model :typeId)
                                          (hh/from :component_type_view))]]))
                 (-> (hh/select [:modelId :model] [:id :typeId])
                     (hh/from :branched_component_type)
                     (hh/where (pq/and (branch-tables/by-branch-id ctx)
                                       [:not [:in [:composite :modelId :id branch-tables/branch-column]
                                              (-> (hh/select :model :typeId branch-tables/branch-column)
                                                  (hh/from :branched_component_type_view))]]))))))

(defn component-types-with-divergent-data! [ctx]
  (let [models (entity/query! model-repo/config ctx pq/all)
        component-types-by-model-id (->> pq/all
                                         (entity/query! component-type-repo/config ctx)
                                         (group-by :modelId))]
    (reduce (fn same-data? [problems model]
              (let [component-entries (model-util/component-entries model)
                    component-types (get component-types-by-model-id (core/id model))
                    component-types-by-typeId (medley/index-by :id component-types)
                    bad-data (remove
                              (fn equal-entry? [{:keys [id] :as component-entry}]
                                (let [component-type (get component-types-by-typeId id)]
                                  (=
                                   (dissoc (component-type-util/prune component-entry)
                                           ;; none of these should have `parent` but some do...
                                           :parent)
                                   (component-type-util/->model-entry component-type))))
                              component-entries)
                    parents-dont-match
                    (mapcat (fn [{parent-typeId :id
                                  children :children :as component-entry}]
                              (keep (fn [child-typeId]
                                      (let [parent-in-component-type
                                            (:parent (get component-types-by-typeId child-typeId))]
                                        (when (not= parent-in-component-type parent-typeId)
                                          {:parent-in-model-root parent-typeId
                                           :parent-in-component-type parent-in-component-type
                                           :component-entry-in-model-root component-entry})))
                                    (map name (keys children))))
                            component-entries)]
                (if (and (empty? bad-data) (empty? parents-dont-match))
                  problems
                  (conj problems {:model-id (core/id model)
                                  :bad-data bad-data
                                  :parents-dont-match parents-dont-match}))))
            nil
            models)))

(defn component-types-with-broken-image-attachment-uris! [ctx]
  (let [component-types (entity/query! component-type-repo/config ctx pq/all)
        has-image? (fn [{image-uri :image :as component}]
                     (and (some? image-uri)
                          (not (str/blank? image-uri))))
        attachment-id-is-not-_id? (fn [{image-uri :image :as component}]
                                    (let [;; See `attachment-service/attachment->uri` to see how segments are created
                                          uri-segments (str/split image-uri #"/")
                                          attachment-id (last uri-segments)]
                                      ((complement core/id?) attachment-id)))]
    (filter #(and (has-image? %)
                  (attachment-id-is-not-_id? %))

(defn usable-color?
  "True when `color` is a non-blank color the frontend can actually render."
  [color]
  (and (not (str/blank? color))
       (or (specs/hex-color? color)
           (specs/allowed-named-css-color? color)
           (specs/rgba-css-color? color))))

(defn component-types-with-color-issues!
  "A blank `color` makes the frontend fall back to the hierarchy-level color; an unrecognized
  (non-blank, malformed) `color` is passed through as-is and renders unstyled. Returns the full
  component-type row plus `:issue`, so callers can act on a violation without a second fetch."
  [ctx]
  (->> (entity/query! component-type-repo/config ctx pq/all)
       (keep (fn [{:keys [color] :as component-type}]
               (cond
                 (str/blank? color) (assoc component-type :issue :missing)
                 (not (usable-color? color)) (assoc component-type :issue :invalid))))))

(defn reference-types-only-in-model! [ctx]
  (pg/execute! (:org-ds ctx)
               (if (branch-context/on-master? ctx)
                 (-> (hh/select :model :typeId)
                     (hh/from :reference_type_view)
                     (hh/where [:not [:in [:composite :model :typeId]
                                      (-> (hh/select :modelId :id)
                                          (hh/from :reference_type))]]))
                 (-> (hh/select :model :typeId)
                     (hh/from :branched_reference_type_view)
                     (hh/where (pq/and (branch-tables/by-branch-id ctx)
                                       [:not [:in [:composite :model :typeId branch-tables/branch-column]
                                              (-> (hh/select :modelId :id branch-tables/branch-column)
                                                  (hh/from :branched_reference_type))]]))))))

(defn reference-types-not-in-model! [ctx]
  (pg/execute! (:org-ds ctx)
               (if (branch-context/on-master? ctx)
                 (-> (hh/select [:modelId :model] [:id :typeId])
                     (hh/from :reference_type)
                     (hh/where [:not [:in [:composite :modelId :id]
                                      (-> (hh/select :model :typeId)
                                          (hh/from :reference_type_view))]]))
                 (-> (hh/select [:modelId :model] [:id :typeId])
                     (hh/from :branched_reference_type)
                     (hh/where (pq/and (branch-tables/by-branch-id ctx)
                                       [:not [:in [:composite :modelId :id branch-tables/branch-column]
                                              (-> (hh/select :model :typeId branch-tables/branch-column)
                                                  (hh/from :branched_reference_type_view))]]))))))

(defn reference-types-with-divergent-data! [ctx]
  (let [models (entity/query! model-repo/config ctx pq/all)
        reference-types-by-model-id (->> pq/all
                                         (entity/query! reference-type-repo/config ctx)
                                         (group-by :modelId))]
    (reduce
     (fn divergent-data? [problems model]
       (let [reference-entries (model-util/reference-entries model)
             reference-types (get reference-types-by-model-id (core/id model))
             reference-types-by-typeId (medley/index-by :id reference-types)
             new-problems
             (->> reference-entries
                  (keep
                   (fn divergent-entry? [{:keys [id] :as reference-entry}]
                     (let [reference-type (get reference-types-by-typeId id)]
                       (when (not=
                              ;; If a `reference-entry`has a `nil` value the key is sometimes
                              ;; omitted.
                              (select-keys reference-type (keys reference-entry))
                              (reference-type-util/prune reference-entry))
                         id))))
                  seq)]
         (if new-problems
           (conj problems {:model-id (core/id model) :reference-ids new-problems})
           problems)))
     nil
     models)))

(defn model-ids-with-broken-or-missing-implicit-reference-type! [ctx]
  (let [non-template-model-ids (->> (entity/query! model-repo/config ctx pq/all [:_id])
                                    core/id-set)
        model-id->reference-types (->> (entity/query! reference-type-repo/config ctx pq/all)
                                       (group-by :modelId))
        has-valid-implicit-reference-type? (fn [model-id]
                                             (let [reference-types (model-id->reference-types model-id)]
                                               (->> reference-types
                                                    (filter (fn [ref-type]
                                                              (and (= "Implicit" (:name ref-type))
                                                                   (= 2 (:id ref-type)))))
                                                    first
                                                    some?)))]
    (reduce
     (fn [problematic-model-ids model-id]
       (if (has-valid-implicit-reference-type? model-id)
         problematic-model-ids
         (conj problematic-model-ids model-id)))
     #{}
     non-template-model-ids)))

(defn unsupported-arrow-type?
  "Whether `arrow-type` is a value the frontend has no arrow head for. A missing arrow type is
  not one of them — `metamodel-service-v2` serves it as \"none\", i.e. a line without a head."
  [arrow-type]
  (and (some? arrow-type)
       (not (contains? model-repo/valid-arrow-types arrow-type))))

(defn reference-types-with-invalid-arrow-types! [ctx]
  (->> (entity/query! reference-type-repo/config ctx pq/all)
       (filter (fn [{:keys [lineBeginning lineEnding] :as reference-type}]
                 (or (unsupported-arrow-type? lineBeginning)
                     (unsupported-arrow-type? lineEnding))))))

(defn model-templates-with-invalid-arrow-types! [ctx]
  (->> (entity/query! model-template-repo/config ctx pq/all)
       (filter (fn [{:keys [referenceTypes]}]
                 (some (fn [{:keys [lineBeginning lineEnding]}]
                         (or (unsupported-arrow-type? lineBeginning)
                             (unsupported-arrow-type? lineEnding)))
                       (vals referenceTypes))))))

(defn- field->arrow-type-counts
  "How often each unsupported value occurs, per field, so a failing check says what to fix
  and where."
  [reference-types]
  (let [unsupported-frequencies (fn [arrow-types]
                                  (frequencies (filter unsupported-arrow-type? arrow-types)))]
    {:lineBeginning (unsupported-frequencies (map :lineBeginning reference-types))
     :lineEnding (unsupported-frequencies (map :lineEnding reference-types))}))

(defn run-integrity-checks! [ctx]
  [{:description "model.root hierarchy is consistent"
    :passed? (zero? (count (inconsistent-component-type-hierarchies ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All non-template models have a workspace"
    :passed? (zero? (count (unused-models ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All model.root types exist in component_type table"
    :passed? (zero? (count (component-types-only-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All component_type table rows exist in model.root types"
    :passed? (zero? (count (component-types-not-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   (let [divergent-models (component-types-with-divergent-data! ctx)]
     {:description "Attribute values of model.root types are identical to component_type table"
      :passed? (empty? divergent-models)
      :stable? true
      :data (when (seq divergent-models)
              {:model-count (count divergent-models)
               :bad-data-count (reduce + (map (comp count :bad-data) divergent-models))
               :parent-mismatch-count (reduce + (map (comp count :parents-dont-match) divergent-models))})})
   (let [violating-component-types-count (count (component-types-with-broken-image-attachment-uris! ctx))]
     {:description "All component type image (attachment) URIs point to the attachment's _id"
      :passed? (zero? violating-component-types-count)
      :data {:count violating-component-types-count}})
   (let [violating-component-types (component-types-with-color-issues! ctx)]
     {:description "All component types have a usable (non-blank, valid) color"
      :passed? (empty? violating-component-types)
      :data (merge {:count (count violating-component-types)}
                   (when (seq violating-component-types)
                     {:ids (map core/id violating-component-types)
                      :by-issue (frequencies (map :issue violating-component-types))
                      :level-counts (frequencies (map :level violating-component-types))
                      :model-count (count (distinct (map :modelId violating-component-types)))
                      :invalid-color-counts (frequencies (keep #(when (= :invalid (:issue %)) (:color %))
                                                               violating-component-types))}))})
   {:description "All model.referenceTypes exist in reference_type table"
    :passed? (zero? (count (reference-types-only-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All reference_type table rows exist in model.referenceTypes"
    :passed? (zero? (count (reference-types-not-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "Attribute values of model.referenceTypes are identical to reference_type table"
    :passed? (zero? (count (reference-types-with-divergent-data! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All models have an 'Implicit' reference type with type id '2'."
    :passed? (zero? (count (model-ids-with-broken-or-missing-implicit-reference-type! ctx)))}
   (let [violating-reference-types (reference-types-with-invalid-arrow-types! ctx)]
     {:description "All reference_type lineBeginning, lineEnding fields are valid"
      :passed? (empty? violating-reference-types)
      :stable? true
      :data (when (seq violating-reference-types)
              {:count (count violating-reference-types)
               :arrow-type-counts (field->arrow-type-counts violating-reference-types)})})
   (let [violating-model-templates (model-templates-with-invalid-arrow-types! ctx)]
     {:description "All model_template referenceTypes lineBeginning, lineEnding fields are valid"
      :passed? (empty? violating-model-templates)
      :stable? true
      :data (when (seq violating-model-templates)
              {:count (count violating-model-templates)
               :ids (map core/id violating-model-templates)
               :arrow-type-counts (->> violating-model-templates
                                       (mapcat (comp vals :referenceTypes))
                                       field->arrow-type-counts)})})])

             reference-types (get reference-types-by-model-id (core/id model))
             reference-types-by-typeId (medley/index-by :id reference-types)
             new-problems
             (->> reference-entries
                  (keep
                   (fn divergent-entry? [{:keys [id] :as reference-entry}]
                     (let [reference-type (get reference-types-by-typeId id)]
                       (when (not=
                              ;; If a `reference-entry`has a `nil` value the key is sometimes
                              ;; omitted.
                              (select-keys reference-type (keys reference-entry))
                              (reference-type-util/prune reference-entry))
                         id))))
                  seq)]
         (if new-problems
           (conj problems {:model-id (core/id model) :reference-ids new-problems})
           problems)))
     nil
     models)))

(defn model-ids-with-broken-or-missing-implicit-reference-type! [ctx]
  (let [non-template-model-ids (->> (entity/query! model-repo/config ctx pq/all [:_id])
                                    core/id-set)
        model-id->reference-types (->> (entity/query! reference-type-repo/config ctx pq/all)
                                       (group-by :modelId))
        has-valid-implicit-reference-type? (fn [model-id]
                                             (let [reference-types (model-id->reference-types model-id)]
                                               (->> reference-types
                                                    (filter (fn [ref-type]
                                                              (and (= "Implicit" (:name ref-type))
                                                                   (= 2 (:id ref-type)))))
                                                    first
                                                    some?)))]
    (reduce
     (fn [problematic-model-ids model-id]
       (if (has-valid-implicit-reference-type? model-id)
         problematic-model-ids
         (conj problematic-model-ids model-id)))
     #{}
     non-template-model-ids)))

(defn unsupported-arrow-type?
  "Whether `arrow-type` is a value the frontend has no arrow head for. A missing arrow type is
  not one of them — `metamodel-service-v2` serves it as \"none\", i.e. a line without a head."
  [arrow-type]
  (and (some? arrow-type)
       (not (contains? model-repo/valid-arrow-types arrow-type))))

(defn reference-types-with-invalid-arrow-types! [ctx]
  (->> (entity/query! reference-type-repo/config ctx pq/all)
       (filter (fn [{:keys [lineBeginning lineEnding] :as reference-type}]
                 (or (unsupported-arrow-type? lineBeginning)
                     (unsupported-arrow-type? lineEnding))))))

(defn model-templates-with-invalid-arrow-types! [ctx]
  (->> (entity/query! model-template-repo/config ctx pq/all)
       (filter (fn [{:keys [referenceTypes]}]
                 (some (fn [{:keys [lineBeginning lineEnding]}]
                         (or (unsupported-arrow-type? lineBeginning)
                             (unsupported-arrow-type? lineEnding)))
                       (vals referenceTypes))))))

(defn- field->arrow-type-counts
  "How often each unsupported value occurs, per field, so a failing check says what to fix
  and where."
  [reference-types]
  (let [unsupported-frequencies (fn [arrow-types]
                                  (frequencies (filter unsupported-arrow-type? arrow-types)))]
    {:lineBeginning (unsupported-frequencies (map :lineBeginning reference-types))
     :lineEnding (unsupported-frequencies (map :lineEnding reference-types))}))

(defn run-integrity-checks! [ctx]
  [{:description "model.root hierarchy is consistent"
    :passed? (zero? (count (inconsistent-component-type-hierarchies ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All non-template models have a workspace"
    :passed? (zero? (count (unused-models ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All model.root types exist in component_type table"
    :passed? (zero? (count (component-types-only-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All component_type table rows exist in model.root types"
    :passed? (zero? (count (component-types-not-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   (let [divergent-models (component-types-with-divergent-data! ctx)]
     {:description "Attribute values of model.root types are identical to component_type table"
      :passed? (empty? divergent-models)
      :stable? true
      :data (when (seq divergent-models)
              {:model-count (count divergent-models)
               :bad-data-count (reduce + (map (comp count :bad-data) divergent-models))
               :parent-mismatch-count (reduce + (map (comp count :parents-dont-match) divergent-models))})})
   (let [violating-component-types-count (count (component-types-with-broken-image-attachment-uris! ctx))]
     {:description "All component type image (attachment) URIs point to the attachment's _id"
      :passed? (zero? violating-component-types-count)
      :data {:count violating-component-types-count}})
   (let [violating-component-types (component-types-with-color-issues! ctx)]
     {:description "All component types have a usable (non-blank, valid) color"
      :passed? (empty? violating-component-types)
      :data (merge {:count (count violating-component-types)}
                   (when (seq violating-component-types)
                     {:ids (map core/id violating-component-types)
                      :by-issue (frequencies (map :issue violating-component-types))
                      :level-counts (frequencies (map :level violating-component-types))
                      :model-count (count (distinct (map :modelId violating-component-types)))
                      :invalid-color-counts (frequencies (keep #(when (= :invalid (:issue %)) (:color %))
                                                               violating-component-types))}))})
   {:description "All model.referenceTypes exist in reference_type table"
    :passed? (zero? (count (reference-types-only-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All reference_type table rows exist in model.referenceTypes"
    :passed? (zero? (count (reference-types-not-in-model! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "Attribute values of model.referenceTypes are identical to reference_type table"
    :passed? (zero? (count (reference-types-with-divergent-data! ctx)))
    :stable? true}
   {:description "All models have an 'Implicit' reference type with type id '2'."
    :passed? (zero? (count (model-ids-with-broken-or-missing-implicit-reference-type! ctx)))}
   (let [violating-reference-types (reference-types-with-invalid-arrow-types! ctx)]
     {:description "All reference_type lineBeginning, lineEnding fields are valid"
      :passed? (empty? violating-reference-types)
      :stable? true
      :data (when (seq violating-reference-types)
              {:count (count violating-reference-types)
               :arrow-type-counts (field->arrow-type-counts violating-reference-types)})})
   (let [violating-model-templates (model-templates-with-invalid-arrow-types! ctx)]
     {:description "All model_template referenceTypes lineBeginning, lineEnding fields are valid"
      :passed? (empty? violating-model-templates)
      :stable? true
      :data (when (seq violating-model-templates)
              {:count (count violating-model-templates)
               :ids (map core/id violating-model-templates)
               :arrow-type-counts (->> violating-model-templates
                                       (mapcat (comp vals :referenceTypes))
                                       field->arrow-type-counts)})})])

(ns ardoq.service.metamodel-sync-service
  "Given lists of component types, reference types and fields, this service
   allows creating/updating/deleting the necessary entities and syncing the
   changes to the metamodel (`model` entity in the API).

  The main entry point is `sync!` and the main transformations can be found
  in `sync*!`.

  The service performs diffing to find out which ones to create, update,
  and delete. The changes are performed in a transaction.

  Entities that should be created do not have a regular ardoq :_id since
  they have not been persisted yet. To enable them to refer to one another
  before persistence, the :_id is instead a frontend-generated 'local-id', which
  starts with the prefix 'local-'.

  This service is responsible for mapping between the two kinds of ids.

  Moreover, metamodel sync service simplifies the format of types, fields
  and global fields:
  - Omits the :id's of types
  - Refers to a component type's :parent with the parent's :_id instead of :id
  - Refers to a field's :componentType and :referenceType's with their :_id
    instead of their :id
  - Uses a simplified :transformation instead of :calculatedFieldSettings
    for (global) fields
  - Date (time) fields are collapsed into a single date (time) range field
  - Annotates global fields with info about their concrete field instances
    and the workspaces those appear in

  The service provides functions for reading, updating and deleting
  global fields in this simplified format as well."

(defn- prepare-component-type-diff!
  "Prepares a component type diff for syncing.
  Updates the index of each component type according to their order in the incoming list.
  For the component types to update, annotates them with their missing type ids (:id) from the database.
  For the component types to create, creates new type ids and resolves the :parent references from local ids
  to the fresh type ids."
  [ctx model-id component-types sync-state]
  (trace-service/with-span! ::prepare-component-type-diff! nil
    (let [old-component-types (component-type-service/query! ctx (component-type-repo/by-model-id model-id))
          sync-state (->> old-component-types
                          (core/by-id)
                          (assoc-in sync-state [:old-entities :component-types]))]
      (->> component-types
           (map #(assoc % :modelId model-id))
           (map-indexed (fn [index comp-type] (assoc comp-type :index index)))
           (map metamodel-sync-util/ensure-returns-value)
           (metamodel-sync-util/annotate-with-existing-type-ids old-component-types)
           (map metamodel-sync-util/prune-component-type)
           (metamodel-sync-util/diff :id old-component-types)
           metamodel-sync-util/create-and-resolve-component-type-ids
           (assoc-in sync-state [:diff :component-types])))))

(defn- prepare-reference-type-diff!
  "Prepares a reference type diff for syncing.
  Updates the index of each reference type according to their order in the incoming list.
  For the reference types to update, annotates them with their missing type ids (:id) from the database.
  For the reference types to create, creates new type ids based on the model's :maxReferenceTypeKey."

(ns ardoq.service.component-type-service
  {:team "core"}
  (:require
   [ardoq.core :as core]
   [ardoq.persistence.component-type-repo :as component-type-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.global-field-component-type-repo
    :as global-field-component-type-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.global-field-repo :as global-field-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres-entity :as entity]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres-repo :as repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.postgres :as pg]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.postgres-query :as pq]
   [ardoq.persistence.workspace-repo :as workspace-repo]
   [ardoq.service.authorization-service :as authorization-service]
   [ardoq.service.global-field-service :as global-field-service]
   [ardoq.service.hook-service :as hook-service]
   [ardoq.service.model-service :as model-service]
   [ardoq.service.workspace-authorization :as workspace-auth]
   [ardoq.utils :as util]
   [ardoq.utils.component-type-util :as component-type-util]
   [ardoq.utils.model-utils :as model-util]
   [com.stuartsierra.component :as component]
   [medley.core :as medley]))

(def service-config (merge component-type-repo/config
                           {:service :component-type-service
                            ::authorization-service/policy
                            {:read authorization-service/reader+
                             :overview authorization-service/open
                             :fields-by-type-name authorization-service/reader+
                             :get-usage authorization-service/admin}}))

(defn- bulk-create*! [ctx component-types]
  (some->> component-types
           seq
           (map core/assign-id!)
           (entity/create-many! component-type-repo/config ctx)))

(defn- bulk-update*! [ctx component-types]
  (entity/update-many! component-type-repo/config ctx component-types))

(defn- bulk-delete*! [ctx component-types]
  (some->> component-types
           seq
           component-type-repo/by-component-types
           (entity/delete-by-query! component-type-repo/config ctx)))

;; NOTE: The `bulk-<action>!` functions updates models and that updating
;; models triggers a hook that runs `bulk-<action>*!` to propagate changes
;; to the component types.
;; So, if you just need a simple update of component types *without*
;; updating the associated model, you probably want `bulk-<action>*!` instead.
;; When using the full `bulk-<action>!`, make sure you're not accidentally
;; creating a cycle of model and component type updates.

(defn bulk-create!
  "Creates component types by updating all their respective models.
  Returns the created component types."
  [{:keys [model-service] :as component-type-service} ctx component-types]
  (pg/with-transaction-on-org ctx
    (doseq [[model-id create-comp-types] (group-by :modelId component-types)]
      (let [old-model (model-service/query-one-model-or-org-template! ctx (pq/by-id model-id))
            old-comp-types (entity/query! service-config ctx (component-type-repo/by-model-id model-id))
            updated-comp-types (into old-comp-types create-comp-types)
            updated-model (model-util/recreate-root old-model updated-comp-types)]
        (model-service/update! model-service ctx updated-model)))
    (entity/query! service-config ctx (component-type-repo/by-component-types component-types))))

(defn bulk-update!
  "Updates component types by updating all their respective models.
  Returns the updated component types."
  [{:keys [model-service] :as component-type-service} ctx component-types]
  (pg/with-transaction-on-org ctx
    (doseq [[model-id update-comp-types] (group-by :modelId component-types)]
      (let [old-model (model-service/query-one-model-or-org-template! ctx (pq/by-id model-id))
            updated-type-ids (util/fn-set :id update-comp-types)
            old-comp-types (entity/query! service-config ctx (component-type-repo/by-model-id model-id))
            updated-comp-types (->> old-comp-types
                                    (remove #(contains? updated-type-ids (:id %)))
                                    (into update-comp-types))
            updated-model (model-util/recreate-root old-model updated-comp-types)]
        (model-service/update! model-service ctx updated-model)))
    (entity/query! service-config ctx (component-type-repo/by-component-types component-types))))

(defn bulk-delete!
  "Deletes component types by updating all their respective models.
  Returns the deleted component types."
  [{:keys [model-service] :as component-type-service} ctx component-types]
  (pg/with-transaction-on-org ctx

(defn convert-datetime-field-to-date-field!
  [{:keys [field-service component-service reference-service report-service] :as metamodel-refactor-service}
   ctx
   global-field
   timezone]
  (postgres/with-transaction-on-org ctx
    (doseq [global-sibling (find-global-date-range-sibling-fields! ctx global-field)]
      (let [datetime->date (fn [date-time]
                             (some-> date-time
                                     (util/date-time->date-in-timezone timezone)
                                     str))
            updated-global-sibling (field-service/convert-type-from-datetime-to-date! field-service
                                                                                      ctx
                                                                                      global-sibling
                                                                                      datetime->date)]
        (component-service/convert-custom-field-values! component-service ctx updated-global-sibling datetime->date)
        (reference-service/convert-custom-field-values! reference-service ctx updated-global-sibling datetime->date)
        (report-service/convert-custom-field-column-datatypes! report-service ctx updated-global-sibling)
        (doseq [branched-ctx (branched-ctxs-with-field! ctx global-sibling)]
          (let [branched-global-field (global-field-service/global-field!
                                       branched-ctx
                                       (global-field-repo/by-name (:name global-sibling)))]
            (field-service/convert-type-from-datetime-to-date! field-service

                                                            updated-global-sibling
                                                            datetime->date)
            (reference-service/convert-custom-field-values! reference-service
                                                            branched-ctx
                                                            updated-global-sibling
                                                            datetime->date)))))))

(defn- copy-attachments! [{:keys [id-map source-data target-ctx target-data] :as copy-ctx}]
  (let [source-attachments (:attachment source-data)
        target-attachments-by-id (core/by-id (:attachment target-data))]
    (->> source-attachments
         (keep (fn [old-attachment]
                 (when-let [new-attachment (get target-attachments-by-id (id-map (core/id old-attachment)))]
                   (let [old-store (:store old-attachment)
                         new-store (:store new-attachment)]
                     {:bucket (:bucket old-store)
                      :key (:key old-store)
                      :destination-bucket-name (:bucket new-store)
                      :destination-key (:key new-store)}))))
         (attachment-service/bulk-copy-attachments! target-ctx))))

(defn- store-fields!
  [{:keys [service target-data] :as copy-ctx}
   target-ctx-with-same-transaction
   model->old->new]
  (when-let [fields (some->> (seq (:field target-data))
                             (map (fn [{:keys [model] :as field}]
                                    ;; mappings might be nil
                                    (let [mappings (get model->old->new model)]
                                      (update field :referenceType (partial map (fn [v] (get mappings v v))))))))]
    (field-service/bulk-create-without-validation!
     (:field-service service) target-ctx-with-same-transaction fields)))

(defn first-non-conflicting-id [existing-id-set current-id]
  {:pre [(set? existing-id-set)]}
  (if (existing-id-set current-id)
  ;; derive a new id in a similar way to how its done in `model-util/extend-with-reference`
    (inc (apply max existing-id-set))
    current-id))

  (reduce (fn [{:keys [existing-ids-in-model] :as acc} {:keys [id] :as rt}]
            (let [id' (first-non-conflicting-id existing-ids-in-model id)
                  rt' (cond-> rt (not= id id') (assoc :id id' :index id'))]
              (-> (cond-> acc
                    (not= id id') (update :old->new merge {(str id)
                                                           (str id')}))
                  (update :reference-types conj rt')

                             (model-query-service/query! target-ctx)
                             core/by-id)
        adjusted-copied-fields (map #(field-util/remove-non-existing-type-ids (model-id->model (:model %)) %)
                                    copied-fields)
        adjusted-previously-installed-fields (adjust-previously-installed-fields! target-ctx copy-ctx)]
    ;; Will adjust field applicability. However, it'll also make sure that global fields is in sync

(defn- recreate-model-from-types! [ctx model-id]
  (let [comp-types (component-type-service/query! ctx (component-type-repo/by-model-id model-id))
        ref-types (reference-type-service/query! ctx (reference-type-repo/by-model-id model-id))
        model (model-query-service/query-one-raw! ctx (pq/by-id model-id))
        new-model (-> model
                      (model-util/recreate-root comp-types)
                      (model-util/recreate-referenceTypes ref-types)
                      (model-util/helpfully-update-max-ref-types)
                      (model-util/force-max-ref-types-when-empty))]
    (if model
      (crud-service/default-update! model-service/service-config ctx new-model)
      (log/with-context+ {:model-id model-id}
        (log/error "Trying to recreate-model-from-types! but model is missing!")))))

    (recreate-model-from-types! ctx model-id)))

(defn- store-permissions!
  "Persists copied permission documents via `permission-service/create-many!` so
   their `permission_entry` rows are dual-written. Excluded from `do-store-batch!`
   for this reason."
  [target-ctx {:keys [permission]}]
  (permission-service/create-many! target-ctx permission))

(defn- cross-org-field-invariants
  "Prepares a global field for an `equivalent-invariants?` comparison across orgs.
  Expands the calculated-field settings (so a calculated field isn't read as
  equivalent to a non-calculated one), but blanks the stored-query id: it's an
  org-specific reference that never matches across orgs, so we compare
  calculated-ness, not the concrete id. Without this, reusing any stored-query
  calculated global field that already exists in the target org would always throw."
  [global-field]
  (let [expanded (global-field-service/expand-calculated-field-settings global-field)]
    (cond-> expanded
      (get-in expanded [:calculatedFieldSettings :storedQueryId])
      (assoc-in [:calculatedFieldSettings :storedQueryId] ::cross-org-stored-query))))

(defn- store-global-fields!
  "Global fields referenced by an entity-group's `globalFieldIds` are matched to
  the target org by name: an existing target global field is reused (the copied
  id is remapped to the target id), a missing one is created. Returns an id remap
  `{copied-global-field-id -> target-global-field-id}` to apply to the rest of
  `target-data` so entity-group `globalFieldIds` point at the target's ids."
  [target-ctx global-fields]
  (when (seq global-fields)
    (let [existing-by-name (->> (global-field-service/query! target-ctx
                                                             (global-field-repo/by-names (map :name global-fields)))
                                (medley/index-by :name))
          {reuse true create false} (group-by (comp some? existing-by-name :name) global-fields)
          created (when (seq create)
                    ;; Copied fields are in collapsed form (a `:storedQueryId` column); expand
                    ;; them so `bulk-create!`'s internal collapse reconstructs the calculated-field
                    ;; settings instead of nilling `:storedQueryId`.
                    (global-field-service/bulk-create!
                     target-ctx (map global-field-service/expand-calculated-field-settings create)))]
      ;; Reuse the same-named target field only if it's equivalent. `equivalent-invariants?`
      ;; is the field subsystem's own compatibility rule (the one `compatible-with-global-field?`
      ;; uses): type, label, defaultValue, list options, calculated-ness, etc. — not just type.
      ;; See `cross-org-field-invariants` for why the stored-query id is normalized out first.
      (doseq [gf reuse
              :let [target-gf (existing-by-name (:name gf))]]
        (when-not (field-util/equivalent-invariants?
                   (cross-org-field-invariants gf)
                   (cross-org-field-invariants target-gf))
          (client-util/throw
           ::client-util/asset-copy-incompatible-global-field
           {:name (:name gf)})))
      (merge
       (into {} (map (fn [gf] [(core/id gf) (core/id (existing-by-name (:name gf)))])) reuse)
       (zipmap (map core/id create) (map core/id created))))))

(defn- store-data!
  [{:keys [dry-run? target-ctx target-data workspacefolder-id->new-content
           fine-grained-metamodel-copy? target-model-ids] :as copy-ctx}]
  (let [target-ctx'
        ;; Don't calculate calc. fields just yet, because they are not fully in the DB until the transaction commits
        (calculated-field-service/skip-recalculation target-ctx)]
    (trace-service/with-span! ::store-data! nil
      (if dry-run?
        copy-ctx
        (let [copy-ctx
              (postgres/with-transaction-on-org
                target-ctx'
                ;; Write order is a contract with grl, not just FK ordering. Constraints are
                ;; deferrable, so Postgres commits regardless of order, but Debezium emits CDC
                ;; events in WAL write order. The grl consumer looks up a component's parent
                ;; type via type-index; if a :component event precedes its :component_type
                ;; event, the type resolves to nil and grr throws "Label can not be null".
                ;; Keep parent types/fields written before components/references, and tags
                ;; after them (tags reference component/reference ids). See ARD-26877.
                (doseq [[entity-type entities] (dissoc target-data
                                                       :field :reference-type
                                                       :permission :global-field :entity-group
                                                       :component :reference :tag)]
                  (do-store-batch! target-ctx' entity-type entities))
                (when-not fine-grained-metamodel-copy?
                  (doseq [model (:model target-data)]
                    (component-type-service/create-from-model! target-ctx' model)
                    (reference-type-service/create-from-model! target-ctx' model)))
                (store-permissions! target-ctx' target-data)
                ;; Entity groups are stored after their global fields: each referenced global field is
                ;; matched to the target org by name (reused or created), then the resulting id remap
                ;; rewrites the entity groups' globalFieldIds to the target ids before they're stored.
                ;; globalFieldIds only ever live on entity groups, so only that slice is walked.
                (when-let [entity-groups (seq (:entity-group target-data))]
                  (let [global-field-id-remap (store-global-fields! target-ctx' (:global-field target-data))]
                    (do-store-batch! target-ctx' :entity-group
                                     (walk/postwalk-replace global-field-id-remap entity-groups))))
                (let [model-id->old->new (store-reference-types! copy-ctx target-ctx')]
                  (store-fields! copy-ctx target-ctx' model-id->old->new)
                  (when-not fine-grained-metamodel-copy?
                    (global-field-component-type-service/bulk-create-from-fields! target-ctx' (:field target-data))
                    (global-field-reference-type-service/bulk-create-from-fields! target-ctx' (:field target-data)))
                  (when-let [components (seq (:component target-data))]
                    (do-store-batch! target-ctx' :component components))
                  (when-let [references (seq (:reference target-data))]
                    (do-store-batch! target-ctx' :reference references))
                  (when-let [tags (seq (:tag target-data))]
                    (do-store-batch! target-ctx' :tag tags))
                  (doseq [[workspacefolder-id new-content] workspacefolder-id->new-content]
                    (update-workspacefolder! target-ctx' workspacefolder-id new-content))
                  (if fine-grained-metamodel-copy?
                    (do
                      (recreate-models-from-types! target-ctx' target-model-ids)
                      (medley/assoc-some copy-ctx :adjusted-installed-fields (adjust-fields! target-ctx' copy-ctx)))
                    copy-ctx)))]
          (copy-attachments! copy-ctx)

  "Validates multiple field operations. Returns true | client-utils/error"
  [ctx operations]

                                id->model (medley/index-by core/id models)]
                            (update-vals field-id->model-id #(get id->model %))))
        written-fields (keep (fn [{:keys [action entity new-entity]}]
                               (case action
                                 :create entity
                                 :update new-entity
                                 nil))
                             operations)
        field-name->added-confidential (reactive-field-name->confidential-dependencies! ctx written-fields)]

              (let [model (get field-id->model (core/id entity))

    ;; creating a field that would contradict the field invariant.
    (entity/ensure-valid! (:spec field-repo/view-config) field))

                                                        (:defaultValue (id->old-field (core/id f)))

(defn remove-and-collect-last-known-versions
  "Given a set of entities, removes their last known deleted version (if present) and returns a map of `_id`->`_version`"
  [service ctx entities]
  ;; If we are re-creating anything, we need to check for (and remove) any deleted
  ;; version entries *and* set the version of the newly created entity to the last known version
  (reduce (fn [entity-to-version-map entity]
            (if-let [previously-deleted-version (history-repo/remove-existing-deleted-version-entry! service ctx (core/id entity))]
              (assoc entity-to-version-map (core/id entity) previously-deleted-version)
              entity-to-version-map)) {} entities))

(defn create-entities [{:keys [entity-type] :as service} ctx entities]

    (trace-service/with-span! ::create-entities {:entity-count (count entities)}
      (if (= entity-type :field)
        (create-field-entities! service ctx entities)
        ;; Atomic so a failed recreate can't leave a half-cleaned id.
        (postgres/with-transaction-on-org ctx
          (let [requested-versions (remove-and-collect-last-known-versions service ctx entities)]
            (crud-service/bulk-create! service
                                       (branch-context/requested-version-ctx ctx requested-versions)
                                       entities)))))))

  ([service ctx entities] (update-entities service ctx entities nil))
  ([{:keys [entity-type] :as service} ctx entities pre-fetched-id->old]
  ;; With global fields, if the same field occurs more than once in a given `reset` update payload,

  ;; and then propagate changes after all updates trigger

  ;; breaks the read-only requirement of calculated fields. We therefore forge the updates to use the current
  ;; calculated field values from the branch

     (case entity-type
       :field

                                                          id->old-field

           (log/infof "Scenario reset: update fields source-of-truth-field id=%s" (core/id source-of-truth-field))

(defn- on-graph-updated!
  "Recalculate the org's calculated fields, now that the graph they read has changed.

  A recalculation's own field write-back must never reach this. The trigger it would raise is
  buffered rather than dropped, so it would rerun the pass, which would raise it again: an
  unbounded loop holding a job worker per affected org. Two properties of the write path happen
  to prevent the announcement today - `set-field-values!` goes through `update-many!` rather
  than the bulk writes, and `update-field-values` announces nothing from inside its own
  transaction - but neither is stated where a reader of those functions would see it, so the
  `:triggered-by` marker `recalculate!` puts on the ctx is what actually enforces it."
  [{:keys [org triggered-by] :as ctx} _data]
  (when (and (not= :calculated-field triggered-by)
             (feature-service/enabled-in-org? org ::feature-service/impact_tmp_reactive-field-recalculation))
    (log/debugf "Reactive field recalculation triggered for org %s" (:label org))
    (metrics-service/prom-inc! metrics-service/registry
                               ::metrics-service/calculated-field-reactive-trigger
                               {:org (:label org)
                                :outcome (name (:result (schedule-recalculation-of-all-fields! ctx)))}
                               1)))

"Takes similar inputs as [[set-field-values!]] and returns
  `{:changed-fields {<field|_id> <value>}, :updated-component <whole comp.>}`, where changed-fields include any
  reactive fields that have a new value (i.e. depend on the changed value of `field`).

  It does not produce any side effects."
  [branch-ctx field new-values comp-id->field-overrides]
  (let [mainline-ctx (branch-context/->mainline-ctx branch-ctx)
        db-components (->> (pq/by-ids (map :entity-id new-values))
                           (query! mainline-ctx))
        reactive-fields (field-query-service/locally-derived-fields-applicable-to-components!
                         mainline-ctx db-components)]
    (->field-values-with-derived-fields* field new-values comp-id->field-overrides
                                         reactive-fields db-components)))

(defn set-field-values! [{:keys [event-service] :as component-service} ctx field new-values]
  (trace-service/with-span! ::set-component-field-values (count new-values)
    (let [comp-id->partial (field-util/coerce-field-values field new-values)
          ;; Read the current rows UNREDACTED. Recalculation may run as a user who cannot see
          ;; some confidential fields (e.g. an integration service account), but the recompute
          ;; must be independent of who triggered it: locally-derived fields have to be computed
          ;; from the real values (not CF-nils), and these originals are the source
          ;; `gather-custom-fields` uses to restore the confidential values the redacted write
          ;; path strips. A redacted read here would miscompute derived fields and wipe CF values.
          raw-db-components (entity/query! component-repo/unredacted-config ctx (pq/by-ids (keys comp-id->partial)))
          id->db-component (medley/index-by core/id raw-db-components)
          ;; NOTE: we have kept `assoc-deps` for backwards compatibility, but it's unlikely that
          ;; the downstream consumers rely on it. A problem for another day
          db-components (component-deps/assoc-deps! ctx component-deps/default-deps raw-db-components)]
      (->> db-components
           (field-util/merge-updates comp-id->partial)
           (maybe-run-locally-derived-field-transformations ctx false)
           (map (partial record-recalculation-time (:user-time ctx)))
           (update-many! component-service (repo/calculated-field-ctx ctx) id->db-component)
           (event-service/publish-events! event-service ctx :update)
           (hook-service/run-hooks! hook-service/hooks ctx ::hook-service/components-updated)
           count))))

(defn with-custom-field
  "Return a map from component _id to custom field value for the given `field`.

  (Faster than fetching the whole row.)"

(ns ardoq.migration.migration-service
  {:team "core"}
  (:require
   [ardoq.core :as core]
   [ardoq.job.policy :as policy]
   [ardoq.job.runner :as runner]
   [ardoq.job.scheduler :as scheduler]
   [ardoq.logger :as log]
   [ardoq.migration.clj-evaluator :as clj-evaluator]
   [ardoq.migration.migration-files :as migration-files]
   [ardoq.migration.migration-repo :as migration-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.organization-repo :as org-repo]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres-entity :as entity]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.postgres :as postgres]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres.postgres-query :as pq]
   [ardoq.service.housekeeping-service :as housekeeping-service]
   [ardoq.service.postgres-service :as postgres-service]
   [ardoq.utils :as util]
   [clj-time.core :as t]
   [clojure.set :as set]
   [medley.core :as medley]
   [next.jdbc :as jdbc]))

(def job-kw :ardoq.migration/db-migration)

(defn ensure-migration-table-exists! [ds]
  (jdbc/execute! ds [migration-repo/create-sql]))

(defn applied-ids! [ds]
  (util/fn-set :id (postgres/execute! ds migration-repo/applied-ids)))

(defn- unapplied-migrations! [ds migrations]
  (let [applied-ids (applied-ids! ds)]
    (seq (remove (comp applied-ids :id) migrations))))

(defn- insert! [ds id created-at]
  (postgres/execute! ds (migration-repo/insert id created-at)))

(defn- run-sql-migration! [ds {:keys [id sql-statement sql-file-path] :as migration}]
  (util/ensure! sql-statement (format "%s doesn't exist" sql-file-path))
  (jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
    (jdbc/execute! tx [sql-statement])
    (insert! tx id (t/now))))

(defn- run-clj-migration! [ds {:keys [id fn] :as migration} system arg]
  (fn system arg)
  (insert! ds id (t/now)))

(defn- run-noop-migration! [ds {:keys [id] :as migration}]
  (insert! ds id (t/now)))

(defn- migratable-org-ctxs! [ardoq-ds customers-ds housekeeping-service]
  (->> (entity/query! org-repo/config {:ardoq-ds ardoq-ds} pq/all)
       (filter (fn [org]
                 (postgres-service/org-schema-exists? {:customers-ds customers-ds} (:label org))))
       (map (fn [org]
              (housekeeping-service/org-label->ctx housekeeping-service (:label org))))
       (doall)))

(defn eval-code [edn-migrations]
  (->> edn-migrations
       (map (fn [migration-spec]

(s/fdef restore-reference* :args (s/cat :service map?
                                        :ctx ::specs/minimal-ctx
                                        :ref ::postgres-history/versioned-record))
(defn restore-reference*
  "Given an entity version of a reference, restore it"
  [{:keys [event-service] :as restore-service} ctx ref]
  (when (linked-components-exists? ctx ref)
    (when-let [reference (restore-entity! ctx reference-repo/config ref)]
      (->> reference
           (reference-service/post-read)
           (event-service/publish-event! event-service ctx :create)
           (tag-repo/by-reference)
           (find-tags-to-reapply ctx)
           (map (partial re-apply-tag reference))
           (save-tags ctx))
      (log/debug "Restored reference " (core/id reference)))))

(defn can-component-be-restored?
  "Checks that a component can be restored according to current product requirements"
  [component workspace-id model-id type-id parent-id]
  (and component workspace-id model-id type-id
       (= (:rootWorkspace component) workspace-id)
       (= (:model component) model-id)
       (= (:typeId component) type-id)
       (= (:parent component) parent-id)))

(defn reason-component-cannot-be-restored
  "The opposite of can-component-be-restored?, returning the reason why in case it fails"
  [component workspace-id model-id type-id parent-id]
  (when-not (can-component-be-restored? component workspace-id model-id type-id parent-id)
    (cond
      (nil? workspace-id)
      "This component can't be restored because its workspace no longer exists."

      (nil? type-id)
      "This component can't be restored because its component type no longer exists."

      ;; TODO: support restore of ancestors
      (nil? parent-id)
      "This component can't be restored because it is a child of a component that no longer exists."

      :else
      (throw (ex-info "Component cannot be restored, missing explanation."
                      {:component component
                       :workspace-id workspace-id
                       :model-id model-id
                       :type-id type-id
                       :parent-id parent-id})))))

(defn restore-component-no-refs!
  "Restores a component along with its tags. Nothing else."
  [{:keys [event-service] :as restore-service} ctx
   {:keys [_id] :as comp-to-restore}]
  (if-let [restored-entity (restore-entity! ctx component-repo/unredacted-config comp-to-restore)]
    (do (->> (find-tags-to-reapply ctx (tag-repo/by-component comp-to-restore))
             (map (partial re-apply-tag comp-to-restore))
             (save-tags ctx))
        (let [component-with-deps (->> [restored-entity]
                                       (component-deps/assoc-deps! ctx component-deps/default-deps)
                                       first)]
          (event-service/publish-event! event-service ctx :create component-with-deps)))
    (log/warn (str "Could not find " _id " in history"))))

(defn can-reference-be-restored?
  "Checks that a reference can be restored according to current product requirements"
  [reference source-id target-id model-id type-id]
  (and reference source-id target-id type-id model-id
       (= (:source reference) source-id)
       (= (:target reference) target-id)
       (= (:model reference) model-id)
       (= (:type reference) type-id)))

(defn reason-reference-cannot-be-restored
  "The opposite of can-reference-be-restored?, returning the reason why in case it fails"
  [reference workspace-id source-id target-id model-id type-id]
  (when-not (can-reference-be-restored? reference source-id target-id model-id type-id)
    (cond
      (nil? workspace-id)
      "This reference can't be restored because its workspace no longer exists."

      (nil? type-id)
      "This reference can't be restored because its reference type no longer exists."

      (or (nil? source-id) (nil? target-id))
      "This reference can't be restored because its source or target no longer exists."

      :else
      (throw (ex-info "Reference cannot be restored, missing explanation."
                      {:reference reference
                       :source-id source-id
                       :target-id target-id
                       :model-id model-id
                       :type-id type-id})))))

(defn restore-component*
  "Restores a component along with any references and tags. Recursively restores parent if missing."

(defn can-component-be-restored?
  "Checks that a component can be restored according to current product requirements"
  [component workspace-id model-id type-id parent-id]
  (and component workspace-id model-id type-id
       (= (:rootWorkspace component) workspace-id)
       (= (:model component) model-id)
       (= (:typeId component) type-id)
       (= (:parent component) parent-id)))

  "The opposite of can-component-be-restored?, returning the reason why in case it fails"
  [component workspace-id model-id type-id parent-id]
  (when-not (can-component-be-restored? component workspace-id model-id type-id parent-id)
    (cond
      (nil? workspace-id)
      "This component can't be restored because its workspace no longer exists."

      (nil? type-id)
      "This component can't be restored because its component type no longer exists."

      ;; TODO: support restore of ancestors
      (nil? parent-id)
      "This component can't be restored because it is a child of a component that no longer exists."

# Global types

Tracking the remaining work to global types.

Global types means types not bound to the model. The end state is `component_type` / `reference_type` rows that exist
per-org (or wider), not per-model — so a type can be referenced from any workspace's model instead of duplicated into
each one.

This plan does **not** get all the way there. It covers some steps only. Dropping `modelId` from the type tables — the
actual "global" step — is downstream of this plan and only becomes tractable once every consumer reads types via the FK
instead of the model JSON.

## Resolve `componentTypeId` / `referenceTypeId` on insert/update

A helper, not the global-types step itself: it makes component / reference rows actually point at the type tables
instead of carrying the type only as the legacy `(model, typeId)` pair. The type tables are still per-model — this just
wires up the FK on the writing side.

The schema is in place but the data is not:

- Columns `component.componentTypeId` and `reference.referenceTypeId` exist (nullable, `VARCHAR(24)`), with FKs
  `component_componentTypeId_fkey` / `reference_referenceTypeId_fkey` to the type tables. Mirrored on the `__history`
  tables (no FKs there).
- Same columns exist on `branched_component` / `branched_reference`, **but their FKs to the type tables have been
  intentionally dropped** (migration `fix-branched-type-foreign-keys-drop`, [PR
  #13993](https://github.com/ardoq/ardoq-api/pull/13993)) because they broke scenario creation. Branched twins of the
  link tables still exist.

Why scenarios broke? The mainline FK works fine. The branched-side FK doesn't, because the metamodel doesn't ride the
same branching machinery as components/references:

- `branched_component` is populated by a raw `INSERT … SELECT FROM component` that **preserves the mainline `_id`** (and
  therefore the mainline `componentTypeId` value) —
  [`aggregation.clj:41`](../../src/ardoq/persistence/postgres/branch/aggregation.clj#L41).
- `component_type` / `reference_type` are **not** in [`branched-configs`](../../src/ardoq/branch/branch_service.clj#L60)
  and not in [`scope-resolver`'s output](../../src/ardoq/service/scope_resolver.clj#L98). Branched type rows appear
  because creating a branched `model` fires
  [`after-model-but-before-types-created`](../../src/ardoq/service/component_type_service.clj#L142), which recreates
  types from `model.root` via `bulk-create*!` — which calls `core/assign-id!`
  ([`component_type_service.clj:35`](../../src/ardoq/service/component_type_service.clj#L35), same in
  `reference_type_service`). **Each branched type row gets a fresh `_id`.**

So `branched_component.componentTypeId` carries the mainline type `_id`, but the row it should point at in
`branched_component_type` has a different `_id`. The composite FK `(__branch_id, componentTypeId) →
branched_component_type(__branch_id, _id)` added in
[`fix-branched-type-foreign-keys.sql`](../../resources/migrations/org_db_sqls/fix-branched-type-foreign-keys.sql)
violated on every scenario creation; dropping it
([`fix-branched-type-foreign-keys-drop.sql`](../../resources/migrations/org_db_sqls/fix-branched-type-foreign-keys-drop.sql))
unblocked scenarios.

The original (non-branched) FK `component.componentTypeId → component_type(_id)` is fine.

How to proceed?

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

1. **Make derived data preserve mainline `_id` on branch.** Add `component_type` / `reference_type` to
   `branched-configs` and to scope data, sync them via the same `INSERT … SELECT` path as components (preserving `_id`),
   and stop the model-creation hook from minting fresh `_id`s when running on a branch. Then re-add the composite
   branched FK.
2. **Don't branch the metamodel.** Keep `component_type` / `reference_type` mainline-only.
   `branched_component.componentTypeId` FKs back to the mainline `component_type(_id)` (which it already has, since
   branched rows carry mainline `_id`s). The branched type tables and their `_id` divergence go away entirely. Aligned
   with the "types not bound to a model" end state — once types live outside the per-model JSON, the case for forking
   them per scenario is weaker. See [scenarios and the metamodel](https://ardoqcom.atlassian.net/wiki/x/EoAcCgE).

## Add `:componentTypes` / `:referenceTypes` to scope data

Similar to [field cleanup](./field-cleanup.md#add-new-tables-to-scope-data).

## Reconstruct `model.root` / `model.referenceTypes` in branch contexts

On mainline, `model-query-service` overwrites `:root` /
`:referenceTypes` on the returned model by reading from `component_type`
/ `reference_type` via
[`recreate-root-from-component-types`](../../src/ardoq/utils/model_utils.clj#L653).
On branch contexts (including `:branch-view`) the enrichment is **gated
off** —
[`model_query_service.clj:55`](../../src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj#L55)
and
[`:93`](../../src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj#L93):
`(if (branch-context/on-master? ctx) models-with-added-types ;; still needs work models)`.
Callers in a branch ctx get the model row's raw JSON, snapshotted at
branch creation.

The result: model and type-table reads disagree in branch-view.
Reproducer ([Slack](https://ardoq.slack.com/archives/CMC0WK13J/p1739884333254929?thread_ts=1739812381.069259&cid=CMC0WK13J)):

1. Empty org. Create a model with type `a` and components of that type.
2. Create a scenario.
3. Add type `b` to the same model on mainline.

Then with `(assoc scenario-ctx :branch-view true)`:

- `(model-service/query! ctx pq/all)` returns only `a` (from the
  branched model's frozen `:root`).
- `(component-type-service/query! ctx pq/all)` returns `a` and `b` —
  the merged-view CTE
  ([`merged_view.clj:96`](../../src/ardoq/persistence/postgres/branch/merged_view.clj#L96))
  keys on `(id, modelId)`, so type `b`'s mainline row falls through.

Removing the `on-master?` gate so reconstruction runs in branch contexts
is the direction. The previous attempt (Sophie Bosio,
[PR #11733](https://github.com/ardoq/ardoq-api/pull/11733),
[#11755](https://github.com/ardoq/ardoq-api/pull/11755)) was closed
unmerged after hitting scenario-test failures. Joe Douglas's suggestion
on the thread: the type-CTE's `mainline-ids` clause should also consider
whether the containing model is itself on-branch.

Todo:

- [ ] Remove the `on-master?` gate at
      [`model_query_service.clj:55,93`](../../src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj#L55).
- [ ] Reconcile the failing scenario tests — likely by teaching
      [`merged_view/type-cte-clauses`](../../src/ardoq/persistence/postgres/branch/merged_view.clj#L96)
      to exclude mainline types whose model is on-branch.

2. **Don't branch the metamodel.** Keep `component_type` / `reference_type` mainline-only.
   `branched_component.componentTypeId` FKs back to the mainline `component_type(_id)` (which it already has, since
   branched rows carry mainline `_id`s). The branched type tables and their `_id` divergence go away entirely. Aligned
   with the "types not bound to a model" end state — once types live outside the per-model JSON, the case for forking
   them per scenario is weaker. See [scenarios and the metamodel](https://ardoqcom.atlassian.net/wiki/x/EoAcCgE).

## Add `:componentTypes` / `:referenceTypes` to scope data

Similar to [field cleanup](./field-cleanup.md#add-new-tables-to-scope-data).

## Reconstruct `model.root` / `model.referenceTypes` in branch contexts

On mainline, `model-query-service` overwrites `:root` /
`:referenceTypes` on the returned model by reading from `component_type`
/ `reference_type` via
[`recreate-root-from-component-types`](../../src/ardoq/utils/model_utils.clj#L653).
On branch contexts (including `:branch-view`) the enrichment is **gated
off** —
[`model_query_service.clj:55`](../../src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj#L55)
and
[`:93`](../../src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj#L93):
`(if (branch-context/on-master? ctx) models-with-added-types ;; still needs work models)`.
Callers in a branch ctx get the model row's raw JSON, snapshotted at
branch creation.

The result: model and type-table reads disagree in branch-view.
Reproducer ([Slack](https://ardoq.slack.com/archives/CMC0WK13J/p1739884333254929?thread_ts=1739812381.069259&cid=CMC0WK13J)):

1. Empty org. Create a model with type `a` and components of that type.
2. Create a scenario.
3. Add type `b` to the same model on mainline.

Then with `(assoc scenario-ctx :branch-view true)`:

- `(model-service/query! ctx pq/all)` returns only `a` (from the
  branched model's frozen `:root`).
- `(component-type-service/query! ctx pq/all)` returns `a` and `b` —
  the merged-view CTE
  ([`merged_view.clj:96`](../../src/ardoq/persistence/postgres/branch/merged_view.clj#L96))
  keys on `(id, modelId)`, so type `b`'s mainline row falls through.

Removing the `on-master?` gate so reconstruction runs in branch contexts
is the direction. The previous attempt (Sophie Bosio,
[PR #11733](https://github.com/ardoq/ardoq-api/pull/11733),
[#11755](https://github.com/ardoq/ardoq-api/pull/11755)) was closed
unmerged after hitting scenario-test failures. Joe Douglas's suggestion
on the thread: the type-CTE's `mainline-ids` clause should also consider
whether the containing model is itself on-branch.

Todo:

- [ ] Remove the `on-master?` gate at
      [`model_query_service.clj:55,93`](../../src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj#L55).
- [ ] Reconcile the failing scenario tests — likely by teaching
      [`merged_view/type-cte-clauses`](../../src/ardoq/persistence/postgres/branch/merged_view.clj#L96)
      to exclude mainline types whose model is on-branch.

(when-let [violations (seq (component-integrity-checks/comp-counter-below-max-component-key ctx))]
    (doseq [{:keys [_id max-key]} violations]
      (postgres/update-by-query!
       {:return-data? false :suppress-versioning? true}
       (:org-ds ctx)
       "workspace"
       [:= :_id _id]
       {:compCounter max-key}))
    (log/infof "Fixed compCounter for %d workspaces where it was below the max component key"
               (count violations))))

(defn fix-orphaned-references!
  "Set orphaned references to type 2 (Implicit) when their reference type no longer exists.
   This fixes data corruption that occurred when reference types were deleted
   while still being referenced by existing references."
  [ctx]
  (when-let [orphaned-ref-ids (seq (core/id-set (reference-integrity-checks/types-resolve-against-tables? ctx)))]
    (let [orphaned-refs (entity/query! reference-repo/config ctx (pq/any :_id orphaned-ref-ids))
          orphaned-by-model (group-by :model orphaned-refs)
          ;; Query all affected models to check if type 2 (Implicit) exists
          model-ids (keys orphaned-by-model)
          models (entity/query! model-repo/config ctx (pq/any :_id model-ids))
          model-id->model (core/by-id models)]
      (when-let [refs-to-update
                 (seq
                  (mapcat
                   (fn [[model-id refs]]
                     (let [model (get model-id->model model-id)
                           has-implicit-type? (contains? (:referenceTypes model) :2)]
                       (if has-implicit-type?
                         (do
                           (log/warnf "Found %d orphaned references in model %s - setting to type 2 (Implicit). IDs: %s"
                                      (count refs)
                                      model-id
                                      (pr-str (core/id-set refs)))
                           (map #(assoc % :type 2) refs))
                         (do
                           (log/warnf (str "Cannot fix %d orphaned references in model %s - "
                                           "type 2 (Implicit) does not exist in model. IDs: %s")
                                      (count refs)
                                      model-id
                                      (pr-str (core/id-set refs)))
                           []))))
                   orphaned-by-model))]
        (entity/update-many! reference-repo/config ctx refs-to-update)
        (log/infof "Set %d orphaned references to type 2 (Implicit)" (count refs-to-update))

(ns ardoq.service.integrity-check-registry
  "Central registry for all data integrity checks in the system.

  ## Two Registries: Global and Per-Org

  The system maintains two separate registries for different scopes of integrity checks:

  - **`registry-global`**: System-wide checks that run with housekeeping context (access to both
    ardoq and ardoq_customers databases). Use for cross-database or system-level validations
    like invalid indices, global configuration, or ardoq database table checks.

  - **`registry-per-org`**: Organization-scoped checks that run per-org with org context. Use for
    customer data validation within a specific organization's schema (components, references,
    workspaces, etc.).

  ## Adding a New Integrity Check

  1. Implement a public `run-integrity-checks!` function in your service namespace:

     ```clojure
     (defn run-integrity-checks! [ctx]
       [{:description \"Components have valid type IDs\"
         :stable? true
         :passed? (every? valid-type-id? components)}])
     ```

  2. Add your check to the appropriate registry:

     ```clojure
     {:group \"my-group\"
      :check-fn my-service/run-integrity-checks!}
     ```

  3. If your check needs access to the full system (rare), mark it with `:requires-system? true`:

     ```clojure
     {:group \"my-group\"
      :check-fn my-service/run-integrity-checks!
      :requires-system? true}  ; check-fn will be called with (system ctx) instead of (ctx)
     ```

  ## Return Format

  Each check function must return a sequence of maps with:
  - `:description` (required) - String describing what the check validates
  - `:passed?` (required) - Boolean indicating if validation passed
  - `:stable?` (optional) - When true, failures log as errors; omit to log as warnings
  - `:data` (optional) - Diagnostic info for failures (keep small, no sensitive data)

  ## Execution

  - **Per-org checks** run nightly per organization via `ardoq.utils.integrity-job-utils/check-job-per-org-kw`
  - **Global checks** run nightly once via `ardoq.utils.integrity-job-utils/check-job-global-kw`
  - Both can be invoked manually via `ardoq.service.integrity-service/lint!` with the appropriate registry"
  (:require
   [ardoq.auth.saml-integrity-checks :as saml-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.branch.branch-integrity-checks :as branch-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.broadcasts.broadcast-integrity-checks
    :as broadcast-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.dashboards.integrity-checks :as dashboard-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.inventory.inventory-integrity-checks
    :as inventory-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.job.integrity-checks :as job-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.permission.integrity-checks :as permission-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.reports.integrity-checks :as report-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.scenarios.scenario-integrity-checks
    :as scenario-integrity-checks]
   [ardoq.service.attachment-folder-service :as attachment-folder-service]
   [ardoq.service.attachment-integrity-checks
    :as attachment-integrity-checks]
