# Nuggets — investigator, 2026-09-16

Context: harvesting undocumented conventions/traps in ardoq-api, checked against CLAUDE.md, test/CLAUDE.md, ai-features.md, backend-coding-conventions.md, README.md, and skill frontmatters first.

Curated by organise-nuggets, 2026-09-16: all 5 verified against the code; 1 narrowed, 2 refined, 1 mechanism corrected; 1 entry added during verification. Consolidated into `ardoq-api/.nuggets`.

## Tests needing a running system must use `ardoq.test.ardoq/deftest` (or `ardoq.test.api/deftest`), not plain `clojure.test/deftest`

- **Kind:** trap
- **Applies to:** `test/` — tests that touch the DB, the handler, or `*ctx*`. NOT a blanket rule (see comment).
- **Source:** test/ardoq/test/ardoq.clj:54-83 (the `deftest` macro wraps the body in `with-system`, binding `*system*`/`*handler*`/`*ctx*`); `.clj-kondo/config.edn:19-20` lints both variants as `clojure.test/deftest`
- **Confidence:** verified — macro definition read in full; usage counted across the test tree
- **Nugget:** A plain `clojure.test/deftest` compiles but binds no system: anything relying on `*ctx*`, `*handler*` or the DB will fail or silently no-op. Use the domain `deftest` for those. Test metadata (`^{:system-config ...}`, `^{:borrowed-system ...}`, `^:unstrument`) is read by this macro only and does nothing on a plain `deftest`.
- **Comment:** Narrowed by organise-nuggets. The original claimed "never plain `clojure.test/deftest`" across all of `test/`; that is wrong — 89 of 773 test files legitimately use plain `deftest` for pure unit tests with no system, against 507 using the `ardoq.test.ardoq`/`ardoq.test.api` variants. The rule is conditional on needing a system, not absolute. Not covered by test/CLAUDE.md, which documents helpers/assertions/mocking but not the macro.

## `:performance`-tagged tests are skipped in CI (kaocha) but still run under plain `lein test`

- **Kind:** test
- **Applies to:** repo-wide test running
- **Source:** tests.edn:6-7 (`:kaocha.filter/skip-meta [:performance]`); .github/workflows/build-and-test.yml:255 (CI runs `lein -o kaocha`); project.clj:244-246,258 (`:kaocha` profile and alias)
- **Confidence:** verified in config and in the CI workflow
- **Nugget:** CI runs `lein kaocha`, which skips any test tagged `^:performance` (allocation/timing tests — run those from the REPL). Plain `lein test` has no such filter and will execute them, so a locally-failing performance test is not necessarily why CI is red, and green CI does not mean it passed.
- **Comment:** `kaocha-retry` is also enabled (tests.edn:11), so CI silently retries failing tests — a flaky test can pass CI without anyone noticing. Currently only `test/ardoq/integrations/spreadsheet/test_references_import_allocations.clj` carries the tag, so the blast radius is small today; the CI/local divergence is the durable part.

## Every reitit route with path params must spec them as an explicit map, or the router fails to compile

- **Kind:** structure
- **Applies to:** all route registration validated through `src/ardoq/router.clj` (the whole route tree)
- **Source:** src/ardoq/router.clj:99-144 (`missing-specs?`, `all-path-params-specced?`, `ardoq-router-validation`)
- **Confidence:** verified — validator read in full
- **Nugget:** `:parameters {:path {...}}` must be a literal map of `:param-name` to a registered spec keyword or a bare predicate fn. A keyword pointing at an `(s/keys ...)` spec is rejected outright, and any path template variable without a matching entry throws at router-compile time (the app fails to boot), not at request time. The stated reason is introspectability without spec-tools.
- **Comment:** Refined by organise-nuggets: the validator exempts the `:options` method and the `/api-docs/*` route (router.clj:119), and accepts `fn?` predicates as well as registered specs.

## Undeclared query/form/body params are unreadable in a handler — `strip-params-middleware` wipes them

- **Kind:** trap
- **Applies to:** every endpoint under the public `""` and `/api` route trees (src/ardoq/route_tree.clj:212, 272-274)
- **Source:** src/ardoq/router.clj:271-297 (`strip-params-middleware`); mount sites src/ardoq/route_tree.clj:204, 212, 274
- **Confidence:** verified — middleware body and both mount sites read
- **Nugget:** Never destructure a param off `request` that is not declared in the route's `:parameters`. `coerce-request-middleware` runs first and moves declared, spec-passing values into `:parameters`; `strip-params-middleware` then sets `:query-params`, `:form-params`, `:body-params` and `:params` to `{}` before the handler sees the request. There is no working "just read it off `:params`" fallback — declared params are the only params. The intent is self-documenting, swagger-accurate endpoints.
- **Comment:** Mechanism corrected by organise-nuggets: the original said the params were gone "by the time coercion runs", which has the order backwards — coercion is the outer middleware and runs before stripping.

## The middleware order in `coerce-multipart-strip-middlewares` is a security fix and must not be reordered

- **Kind:** exception
- **Applies to:** src/ardoq/route_tree.clj — the shared middleware vector used by the `""` and `/api` route trees
- **Source:** src/ardoq/route_tree.clj:202-207 (in-code note: "Updated middleware order as per APPSEC-1642 to address a reported security vulnerability. Ensure any changes maintain the sequence to preserve security fix.")
- **Confidence:** verified — the constraint is stated in the code at the definition site
- **Nugget:** The sequence `coerce-request-middleware` → `multipart-middleware` → `strip-params-middleware` → `wrap-thread-utilization-metrics` is load-bearing for a security fix (APPSEC-1642). Do not reorder it, and do not insert middleware into the middle of it, when adding middleware to those route trees — append instead, and check the ticket if the order seems to be in the way.
- **Comment:** Added by organise-nuggets while verifying the `strip-params-middleware` nugget; not in the original harvest.

## Canonical kondo-enforced aliases: `ardoq.utils` → `util`, `ardoq.utils.request-utils` → `request-util`

- **Kind:** convention
- **Applies to:** repo-wide
- **Source:** .clj-kondo/config.edn:5-7 (`:consistent-alias`); usage at src/ardoq/router.clj:6-7, src/ardoq/auth/api.clj:36
- **Confidence:** verified in config + usage sites
- **Nugget:** Always alias `ardoq.utils` as `util` and `ardoq.utils.request-utils` as `request-util`. Any other alias is a `:consistent-alias` lint failure, not a style preference.

---

## Tombstones (verified wrong — do not re-save)

- ~~"Route handlers must use `ardoq.test.ardoq/deftest`, never plain `clojure.test/deftest`" (scope: all of `test/`)~~ — the absolute form is false: 89 test files correctly use plain `deftest` for system-free unit tests. Kept in narrowed form above. The original title also said "route handlers" for a rule about test namespaces.
- ~~"`strip-params-middleware` wipes params before coercion middleware repopulates `:parameters`"~~ — order is reversed; coercion is outermost and runs first. Conclusion was right, mechanism wrong. Kept in corrected form above.

# Nuggets — investigator, 2026-09-16

Context: investigating which write paths bypass metamodel enforcement in ardoq-api. Checked
`ardoq-api/.nuggets`, `.aispace/nuggets/investigator-20260916-134711.md`, CLAUDE.md and
docs/backend-coding-conventions.md first — no overlap. All line numbers from `origin/master`.

## The metamodel is dual-written: `model.root`/`model.referenceTypes` JSON **and** the `component_type`/`reference_type` tables

- **Kind:** structure
- **Applies to:** any code creating/updating/deleting component or reference types
- **Source:** in-code note at `src/ardoq/service/component_type_service.clj:48-54`; `bulk-create!`/`bulk-update!`/`bulk-delete!` at :56,:69,:85 vs `bulk-create*!`/`bulk-update*!`/`bulk-delete*!` at :33,:38,:41; hooks registered at :130-147
- **Confidence:** verified — full namespace read
- **Nugget:** The two representations are kept in sync in *one* direction only: the `bulk-<action>!` functions rewrite the `model` doc via `model-service/update!`, and the `after-model-but-before-types-{created,updated}` hooks then propagate that into the type tables via the `*`-suffixed functions. Calling a `bulk-<action>*!` directly writes the tables and leaves the `model` JSON stale — no error, no check. Same split exists in `reference_type_service`. Choose the starred variant only when you are already inside the model-update hook, and never create a model↔type update cycle (the code note says exactly this).
- **Comment:** `src/ardoq/service/model_integrity_checks.clj` exists solely because the two sides drift in prod: `component-types-only-in-model!` (:31), `component-types-not-in-model!` (:46), `component-types-with-divergent-data!` (:61), and the reference-type equivalents (:132,:147,:162). `src/ardoq/migration/core/global_types.clj` is the repair kit.

## `model-service/update!` does NOT run the model's `processable?` validators

- **Kind:** trap
- **Applies to:** every caller of `ardoq.service.model-service/update!` (importers, `component_type_service`, `metamodel_sync_service`, migrations)
- **Source:** `src/ardoq/service/model_service.clj:390-403` (`update!` runs only `verify-valid-model-change`, `model-util/validate-model`, `validate-component-type-images!`) vs `:304-318` (`defmethod crud-service/processable? :model-service` → `validate-flexibility`, `validate-removal-of-reference-types`, `validate-adding-reference-type`, `validate-consistent-type-ids`)
- **Confidence:** verified — both definitions read
- **Nugget:** Writing a model through `model-service/update!` skips four validators that only run when a caller explicitly invokes `crud-service/processable?` (the `crud-api/update*` path used by `model_api`). So "can't remove a reference type that is in use", "can't turn a flexible model strict", "reference-type key must be the max" and "type ids are consistent" are **not** enforced on the service-internal paths. Only `verify-valid-model-change` (blocks removing component types that still have components) is unconditional. If you add a model invariant, put it in `update!`, not in `processable?`, or it will not hold.
- **Comment:** `metamodel_sync_service` compensates by hand: it re-checks reference types in use at `src/ardoq/service/metamodel_sync_service.clj:443-460` and calls `crud-service/processable?` explicitly for the flexibility change at :812-815.

## Entity attributes with no matching `field` row are neither rejected nor stripped — they just persist

- **Kind:** trap
- **Applies to:** all component/reference writes except the public `/api/v2` resources
- **Source:** `src/ardoq/utils/field_utils.clj:469-480` (`typecheck!` — `:when field` skips any key without a field definition); `ensure-valid-fields!` at :593-608 is the only field gate in `component-service/bulk-create-sans-events!` / `bulk-update-sans-events!`
- **Confidence:** verified — functions read in full
- **Nugget:** `field-util/typecheck!` only type-checks keys that match a `field` row for the entity's model; unknown keys fall straight through to Postgres. Rejection of undefined custom fields happens *only* in the public v2 layer, via `field-service/custom-field-errors!` (`src/ardoq/service/field_service.clj:1403`, `field-validation-errors` at :1365 → `::client-utils/unknown-field`), called from `src/ardoq/api/public/v2/batch.clj:313` and the v2 component/reference resources. The internal `/api/batch` and any service-level caller can write arbitrary attributes.

## An integrity check without `:stable? true` is a check known to fail in production

- **Kind:** convention
- **Applies to:** reading and adding integrity checks
- **Source:** `src/ardoq/service/integrity_check_registry.clj:47` — "`:stable?` (optional) - When true, failures log as errors; omit to log as warnings"
- **Confidence:** verified — registry docstring read; examples confirmed
- **Nugget:** The presence/absence of `:stable? true` is the repo's marker for "this invariant actually holds" vs "this is a known, tolerated data violation". Do not assume a registered check implies the invariant holds. Currently-unstable examples: "Component field values adhere to field options of list type fields" (`src/ardoq/service/component_integrity_checks.clj:237`), "All component names are non-blank" (:235), "component.componentTypeId is not null" (:245), and the reference equivalents at `src/ardoq/service/reference_integrity_checks.clj:127,131,133`. Checks run nightly per org; they never block a write.

## The metamodel does not ride the branching machinery — model and type-table reads disagree inside a scenario

- **Kind:** trap
- **Applies to:** anything reading types in a branch/scenario context
- **Source:** `docs/plans/global-types.md` ("The result: model and type-table reads disagree in branch-view."); `src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj:55,93` (type re-enrichment gated behind `branch-context/on-master?`); `src/ardoq/persistence/postgres/branch/merged_view.clj:96`
- **Confidence:** verified — doc statement plus the cited gate
- **Nugget:** On mainline, `model-query-service` overwrites `:root`/`:referenceTypes` from the `component_type`/`reference_type` tables. In any branch context that enrichment is switched off, so the caller gets the branched model row's JSON frozen at branch creation, while `component-type-service/query!` returns the merged view including mainline types added after the branch. Branched type rows also get *fresh* `_id`s (the model-creation hook calls `core/assign-id!`), which is why the branched `componentTypeId` FKs were deliberately dropped (`resources/migrations/org_db_sqls/fix-branched-type-foreign-keys-drop.sql`). Don't rely on type `_id` equality across mainline and branch.

content.text:
Report follows. All line numbers are `origin/master`.

## 1. Bulk / batch APIs — **validates** (with two gaps)

**Endpoints.** `/api/batch` → `src/ardoq/route_tree.clj:293` → `src/ardoq/api/batch_api.clj` (v1 create-only shape, converted by `->v2` at `batch_service.clj:~400`) and `/api/batch/v2` → `src/ardoq/api/batch_api_v2.clj`. `/api/v2/batch` → `src/ardoq/api/public/v2/routes.clj:25` → `src/ardoq/api/public/v2/batch.clj`. Engine for all three: `src/ardoq/batch/batch_service.clj`.

**Rule.** Batch is not a side door. `batch-service/execute!` (`batch_service.clj:~365`) interleaves, per stage: `crud-service/every-processable?` on `component-service` and `reference-service` (`batch_service.clj:300-310`) then `component-service/bulk-create-sans-events!` / `bulk-update-sans-events!` / reference equivalents. Those bulk fns are the same validation pipeline the single-entity paths use — `model-service/resolve-component-types!`, `model-service/ensure-valid-fields-many!`, `crud-service/pre-bulk-create-default!` (`component_service.clj:606-630`, `:696-714`). `component-service`'s `every-processable?` (`component_service.clj:528-570`) validates model membership, type legality, parent existence/same-model, self-parent, hierarchy cycles and `legal-hierarchy-error`.

`src/ardoq/batch/validate.clj` is *static only* — duplicates, update-then-delete, unknown/deleted parent-source-target ids, parent cycles. Its own docstring says it "should not need to read from the database or perform other validation that is handled by the crud service."

**Gap A — auto-assigns a component type when `typeId` is absent.** `model-util/resolve-component-type` (`src/ardoq/utils/model_utils.clj:415-427`): with no `typeId` it takes `(first available-types)` for the parent, logging `"Assigning random type to component:"`. Throws `::no-available-child-type` only if the parent has no legal children. This is not type *creation*, but it is unvalidated type *selection*.

**Gap B — `/api/batch` accepts undefined custom fields; `/api/v2/batch` rejects them.** `field-util/typecheck!` (`src/ardoq/utils/field_utils.clj:469-480`) skips any entity key with no matching `field` row (`:when field`), so arbitrary attributes persist. The unknown-field rejection lives only in the public v2 layer: `public/v2/batch.clj:313` → `field-service/custom-field-errors!` (`field_service.clj:1403`) → `::client-utils/unknown-field` (`field_service.clj:1382`). The internal `/api/batch` and `/api/batch/v2` do not call it.

**Not in scope of "metamodel":** `component_api.clj:167` `bulk-delete`, `:457` `partial-bulk-update` (goes through `component-service/bulk-update!` at `:499`), `user_service/bulk_operations.clj` and `authorization_service_bulk.clj` (users/permissions, no metamodel).

## 2. Imports / integrations — **auto-creates** types and fields, then validates entities

**Yes, importers create component types, reference types and fields on the fly.** Functions, in order:

- Component types: `apply-component-types-changes` (`src/ardoq/integrations/spreadsheet/core/model.clj:127`) — new type names collected from the sheet's parent/child pairs, minted with `model-util/gen-comp-id`, merged into `:component-hierarchy`, `:styles`, `:metadata`.
- Reference types: `apply-reference-types-changes` (`same file:105`) — new names get ids from `inc (max-reference-id …)`, plus `ensure-default-reference-type`.
- Both wrapped by `updated-models` (`:196`), called from `models-to-upsert` (`src/ardoq/integrations/spreadsheet/import.clj:136`) and persisted by `model/create-model!` / `model/update-model!` (`core/model.clj:25,31`) at `import.clj:252-254`, i.e. through `model-service/create!` / `update!`.
- Fields: `upsert-fields!` (`import.clj:286`) → `ardoq.integrations.field-utils/execute!` (`src/ardoq/integrations/field_utils.clj:251`) → `update-or-create-field!` (`:169`) → `create-workspace-field!` / `update-workspace-field!` (`:125`, `:116`), both of which call `field-service/ensure-processable!` first.
- Entities: `create-comps-and-refs!` (`import.clj:318`) submits to `batch-service-v2`, so section 1's validation applies.

**Default type name.** A reference column with a create-missing strategy and no configured type falls back to the literal `"Component"` (`src/ardoq/integrations/spreadsheet/defaults.clj:8`, used at `src/ardoq/integrations/tabular/importcontext/missing_components.clj:44`) — which then gets *created* as a type by the step above.

**Tabular / unified importers reuse this.** `src/ardoq/integrations/tabular/tabular_import_service.clj:343-385` (`import!`) delegates to `sheet-upload-service/import-from-{data,cache}!`; the comment at `:351` says "forwards handling to the Excel/CSV importer for now." So spreadsheet, tabular, ServiceNow, cloud-provider and ITPedia all share the one auto-create path. `src/ardoq/integrations/tabular/importconfig/import_config.clj` is mapping/config accessors only — no writes.

**Verdict: auto-creates types and fields (through the validating services), validates entity writes.** The net effect is that no import can violate the model, because the model is widened to fit the import.

## 3. Migrations — **bypasses**

Execution: `src/ardoq/migration/migration_service.clj:39-49` — `:sql true` entries run raw SQL in a transaction; `:fn` entries are arbitrary Clojure `eval`'d by `src/ardoq/migration/clj_evaluator.clj:95-99`; entries with neither are recorded as no-ops (`run-noop-migration!`, `:47`). Run as a nightly/startup job, never through an API or a service gate.

Confirmed model/type/field rewrites without validation:

- `src/ardoq/migration/core/types_fixup.clj:15-21` — rewrites `model.root` component-type names via `entity/update! model-repo/config (repo/non-versioning-ctx ctx)`: no `model-service/update!`, no `verify-valid-model-change`, no version bump, no type-table propagation hook.
- `src/ardoq/migration/core/global_types.clj:21-40` — `populate-reference-types!` / `populate-component-types!` delete *all* rows from `component_type`/`reference_type` plus their `__history` tables and recreate them from models, each step wrapped in `util/ignore-errors`. Comment: `;; we delete all old stuff (noone knows about these anyways)`.
- `global_types.clj:88-114` — `populate-componentTypeIds!` / `populate-referenceTypeIds!` / `unset-componentTypeIds-referenceTypeIds!`: bare `UPDATE component SET "componentTypeId" = …` / `SET … = nil` on the whole table.
- `global_types.clj:72-88` — `remove-invalid-reference-type-from-model!` and `fix-non-string-component-types-in-model!` call `model-service/update!` with `repo/non-versioning-ctx`.
- `src/ardoq/migration/core/misc.clj:241-275` — `fix-orphaned-references!` reassigns references to type `2` via `entity/update-many! reference-repo/config`.
- `src/ardoq/migration/core/fields_fixup.clj:17,26,57,77` — raw `jdbc/execute-one!` / `postgres/execute!` against field data.
- `resources/migrations/org_db_sqls/delete-dangling-models.sql` and `delete-workspaces-without-models.sql` are **0-byte files** still registered in `resources/migrations/org-db-migrations.edn:363,387`.

## 4. Copy / merge / import workspace, scenarios, metamodel sync & refactor

### 4a. Asset copy / bundle install — **bypasses for entities, partially for metamodel**

`src/ardoq/service/asset_copy_service.clj`, `store-data!` at `:1265`. `src/ardoq/service/bundle_service.clj:234` (bundle/solution install) and workspace copy both route here.

- Components, references, tags, workspaces: `do-store-batch!` (`:145`) = `entity/create-many!` on the repo config. **No** `component-service`, no type resolution, no `ensure-valid-fields-many!`, no hierarchy check.
- Fields: `store-fields!` (`:1074`) → `field-service/bulk-create-without-validation!` (`src/ardoq/service/field_service.clj:940`). Its own comment (`:942-945`) states what is skipped: `prepare-create-fields!`, i.e. the global-field invariant (`ensure-global-field-invariant!`) and `remove-non-existing-types!`. Spec validation (`entity/ensure-valid!`) is kept. `initialize-attributes!` is *not* called, so pre-existing target entities get no default values for the copied fields.
- Types: when not `fine-grained-metamodel-copy?`, `component-type-service/create-from-model!` / `reference-type-service/create-from-model!` (`:1291-1292`) — the `*`-suffixed direct table writes, no model update.
- Model: `recreate-model-from-types!` (`:1193`) rebuilds `:root`/`:referenceTypes` from the type tables and writes with `crud-service/default-update! model-service/service-config` (`:1203`) — bypassing `model-service/update!` entirely, so even `verify-valid-model-change` does not run.
- Guarantees it *does* make: `field-util/remove-non-existing-type-ids` per copied field in `adjust-fields!` (`:1170-1191`); cross-org global-field compatibility via `field-util/equivalent-invariants?` throwing `::asset-copy-incompatible-global-field` (`:1247-1260`); reference-type id conflict remapping (`resolve-type-id-conflicts`, `:1094`). Write *order* is a contract with the GraphLake CDC consumer, not just FKs — see the comment at `:1275-1284` (ARD-26877).

### 4b. Template instantiation — **validates**

`workspace_service.clj:354-367` → `model-template-service/->model!` (`src/ardoq/service/model_template_service.clj:87`) → `model-service/create!` + `field-service/create-and-add-id` per field (`:125`). Normal validating services.

### 4c. Scenario / branch — **mixed**

- Branch copy: `branch_service.clj:134-162` — `copy-branch-data!` is a raw `INSERT … SELECT` per branched table (`branch-aggregation/copy-branch-data-aggregation`). Pure row copy, zero validation.
- Branch reset/merge writes: `create-entities` (`:207`) and `update-entities` (`:225`) use `crud-service/bulk-create!` / `bulk-update!` on the real services, i.e. validated; components/references additionally get `model-service/ensure-valid-fields-many!` via `retain-read-only-field-values` (`:219`). Fields use `field-service/bulk-create-preserving-existing-invariants!`.
- **Broken guarantee:** the metamodel does not branch consistently. `docs/plans/global-types.md` states it plainly: `branched_component` is populated by a raw `INSERT … SELECT` preserving the mainline `_id` (and `componentTypeId`), while branched type rows are minted fresh `_id`s by the model-creation hook (`component_type_service.clj:33-35,142`). The composite branched FK therefore violated on every scenario creation and was deliberately dropped (`resources/migrations/org_db_sqls/fix-branched-type-foreign-keys-drop.sql`). Also: type re-enrichment of the model is gated behind `on-master?` (`src/ardoq/service/model_query_service.clj:55,93`), so — quoting the doc — *"The result: model and type-table reads disagree in branch-view."*

### 4d. `metamodel_sync_service` — **validates** (types are source of truth, model derived)

`src/ardoq/service/metamodel_sync_service.clj`. `sync*!` (`:817-840`) runs in a fixed order (comment at `:818-821`): upsert component types → upsert reference types → sync fields → delete component types → delete reference types. All type writes go through `component-type-service/bulk-{create,update,delete}!` / `reference-type-service` equivalents (`:362-364`, `:381-383`, `:439`, `:461`), each of which rewrites the `model` doc via `model-service/update!` (`component_type_service.clj:66,82,97`) — so `verify-valid-model-change` blocks deleting a component type that still has components. Reference-type-in-use is re-checked explicitly at `:443-460` (logs `"Blocked attempt to delete reference types that are in use"`, throws `::reference-types-can't-be-removed`) because `verify-valid-model-change` does not cover reference types. Fields go through `field-service/every-processable?` (`:282`) and the `*-sans-hooks-and-events!` variants (which keep `prepare-create-fields!`, unlike asset copy). Flexibility change calls `crud-service/processable?` explicitly (`:812-815`).

### 4e. `metamodel_refactor_service` — **bypasses entity validation by design**

`src/ardoq/service/metamodel_refactor_service.clj`. The field-type converters (`convert-datetime-field-to-date-field!` `:240`, `convert-text-field-to-checkbox-field!` `:274`, `convert-text-field-to-number-field!` `:305`, and siblings) change the field's `type` first, then rewrite every holding entity via `component-service/convert-custom-field-values!` (`src/ardoq/service/component_service.clj:1029-1037`) and the reference equivalent (`reference_service.clj`). That function does `entity/update-many!` straight to the repo — no `ensure-valid-fields-many!`, no `typecheck!`, no `processable?`. Its docstring states the premise: *"When this runs, the `global-field` and all its instances have been updated in the DB."* Same for `component-service/rename-custom-field!` (`:1024`, raw SQL) and the report/traversal/filter rewrites at `metamodel_refactor_service.clj:198-222`. Also: `postgres/execute!` on `jsonb` filter structures with no spec re-validation. Design intent is documented in `docs/metamodel-refactor-rename-field-strategy.md`.

## 5. GraphLake / Gremlin — **no entity write path; one unvalidated field write-back**

- **GraphLake does not write Ardoq entities.** It is an external RDF store, synced one-way from Postgres: `src/ardoq/graphlake/graphlake_sync_service.clj:33-38` keys orgs on their Postgres schema name; all HTTP verbs in `graphlake_gateway.clj` target GraphLake (`/stores/...`), never Ardoq. `POST /run-update` (`src/ardoq/graphlake/graphlake_api.clj:302`, `graphlake_service.clj:97`, privilege `authorization-service/admin` at `graphlake_service.clj:20`) sends arbitrary SPARQL UPDATE to the GraphLake store — it can corrupt the GraphLake copy with triples violating the ontology, but cannot touch Postgres entities.
- **Gremlin is read-only as a query engine**, but its *results* write field values: `component-service/set-field-values!` (`component_service.clj:974-995`) applies `field-util/coerce-field-values` and then `update-many!` on the repo — **not** `bulk-update-sans-events!`. So calculated-field write-back skips `ensure-valid-fields-many!` and `typecheck!`. The comment at `calculated_field_service.clj:755-762` confirms this routing is relied upon ("`set-field-values!` goes through `update-many!` rather than the bulk writes").
- **`AR-APPSEC-5480-create-gremlin-outside-cf-model.md`**, restricted to what it says about bypassing model/metamodel constraints: it says **nothing** about model or metamodel constraints. Its whole subject is confidential-field redaction — `graph_search/*` result paths never consume `:field-permission/access-context`; the accepted risk is that a holder of `create-gremlin` escalates around CF redaction via free-form Gremlin filters, so redacting graph-search buys nothing. It explicitly records that workspace scoping *is* still enforced (`graph_service.clj:269,301`, `client/gremlin/message.clj:12-24`), i.e. `create-gremlin` is not a cross-workspace pass. No metamodel claim to report.

## 6. Admin / internal endpoints — **read-only, except restore**

- `/internal-api` (`src/ardoq/internal_api_server.clj:738-918`) is metrics and org-copy lifecycle; no model or entity writes. `/api/backoffice` (`route_tree.clj:292`) — no `component-service`/`model-service`/`field-service`/`component-type-service` calls in `backoffice_api.clj`, `backoffice_org_api.clj` or `backoffice_service.clj`.
- Integrity checks and fixups are **not** exposed as endpoints: `src/ardoq/service/integrity_check_registry.clj` says they run nightly per org / globally, or manually via `integrity-service/lint!` from a REPL. `migration_checklist_api.clj` is read-only (`crud-v3/read-only-api`, `:39`).
- **Restore API bypasses.** `src/ardoq/api/restore_api.clj`. Writes go through `restore-service/restore-entity!` (`src/ardoq/service/restore_service.clj:182-192`) = `postgres-history/reinstall` on the repo config — no field typecheck, no hierarchy re-validation.
  - v2 (`restore_api.clj:57-79`, `:81-113`) does check the type still exists, in `:processable?`: `can-component-be-restored?` / `can-reference-be-restored?` (`restore_service.clj:210`, `:256`) compare workspace/model/typeId/parent.
  - **v1 does not.** `restore_api.clj:34-45` sets only `:processable? (fn [_] (nil? entity-to-be-restored))`; `restore-component*` (`restore_service.clj:287`) recursively restores missing parents and calls `restore-entity!` with no type check at all. `restore-reference*` (`:196`) checks only that source and target components exist (`linked-components-exists?`). So `POST /api/restore/component` can reinstate a component whose component type was deleted from the model since.

## Documented allowances for inconsistent data

Exact lines:

1. `src/ardoq/service/model_integrity_checks.clj:75` —
   `;; none of these should have \`parent\` but some do...`
   (inside `component-types-with-divergent-data!`, where `:parent` is dropped before comparing `model.root` entries against `component_type` rows.)

2. `src/ardoq/integrations/spreadsheet/core/model.clj:135` —
   `;; \`:name\` has been an integer instead of a string a few times in prod`
   (hence the `(map str)` on new component-type names.)

3. `src/ardoq/migration/core/misc.clj:242-244` (docstring of `fix-orphaned-references!`) —
   `"Set orphaned references to type 2 (Implicit) when their reference type no longer exists.`
   `This fixes data corruption that occurred when reference types were deleted`
   `while still being referenced by existing references."`

4. `src/ardoq/migration/core/global_types.clj:22` —
   `;; we delete all old stuff (noone knows about these anyways)`
   (before wiping `reference_type` and `reference_type__history`; repeated at `:33` for component types.)

5. `docs/plans/global-types.md` — `The result: model and type-table reads disagree in branch-view.` and, on the branched FKs, `**but their FKs to the type tables have been intentionally dropped** … because they broke scenario creation.`

6. `src/ardoq/service/integrity_check_registry.clj:47` —
   `` - `:stable?` (optional) - When true, failures log as errors; omit to log as warnings ``
   This makes the absence of `:stable? true` the repo's marker for a tolerated violation. Currently tolerated-as-warning, model-relevant: `"Component field values adhere to field options of list type fields"` (`src/ardoq/service/component_integrity_checks.clj:237`), `"All component names are non-blank"` (`:235`), `"component.componentTypeId is not null"` (`:245`), and the reference equivalents at `src/ardoq/service/reference_integrity_checks.clj:127,131,133`. No integrity check ever blocks a write.

7. `src/ardoq/service/model_integrity_checks.clj:117-121` (docstring of `component-types-with-color-issues!`) — `"A blank \`color\` makes the frontend fall back to the hierarchy-level color; an unrecognized (non-blank, malformed) \`color\` is passed through as-is and renders unstyled."`

8. `src/ardoq/service/field_service.clj:942-945`, inside `bulk-create-without-validation!` — `;; This does not contradict the fn name! … The validation that we're referring to here is \`prepare-create-fields!\` which does not allow creating a field that would contradict the field invariant.`

Nothing in `CLAUDE.md` states that data may violate the model; its only relevant text is §"Integrity Checks Framework" (`:245-256`) pointing at the registry.

## Cross-cutting bypass not attributable to one path

`model-service/update!` (`src/ardoq/service/model_service.clj:390-403`) runs only `verify-valid-model-change`, `model-util/validate-model` and `validate-component-type-images!`. The four other model validators — `validate-flexibility`, `validate-removal-of-reference-types`, `validate-adding-reference-type`, `validate-consistent-type-ids` — live in `defmethod crud-service/processable? :model-service` (`:304-318`) and run **only** when a caller invokes `processable?` explicitly. Every service-internal model write (importers, `component_type_service`, `metamodel_sync_service`, migrations) skips them. `asset_copy_service.clj:1203` skips `model-service/update!` too, so it also skips `verify-valid-model-change`.

## Could not determine

- Whether any live `:fn` entry in `resources/migrations/org-db-migrations.edn` currently targets model/type data: the file's model-related entries at `:363,387,666` are `:sql true` or bodyless no-ops, and I did not read all 700+ entries for embedded `fn` forms.
- Whether `component-service/set-field-values!`'s omission of `ensure-valid-fields-many!` is deliberate; no comment states it, and `coerce-field-values` may cover the intended cases.
- Whether the v1 restore endpoints are still reachable from any client (they are registered, but I did not check callers).

Nuggets saved: `/Users/havarddaleng/Documents/git/repos/ardoq/.aispace/nuggets/investigator-20260916-201500.md` (5 entries: the model↔type-table dual-write and `bulk-*!` vs `bulk-*!*` rule, the `model-service/update!` validator gap, unknown-attribute passthrough, `:stable?` semantics, branch/metamodel divergence).
